svg.title: Rolling Window vs Markov Switching
svg.desc: A rolling window depends on an arbitrary window length and cannot avoid lag and ghost effects; Markov switching estimates the number of regimes and the transition probabilities and treats switches as probabilities.
svg.text: A convention that picks a window length vs a model that estimates transition probabilities
None — a summary of the last k
Window length k — chosen by the user
Jumps when an event leaves the window
The number of states K and P
Explicit in the diagonal of P
The estimate jumps as the event leaves the window
Even the end of a regime is judged from the evidence
Change the window and the conclusion changes
The data never tells you which window is right
Parameters and expected duration come out per regime
The model answers duration too — no window length needed
A rolling window hangs on an arbitrary window length and carries lag and ghost effects.
Markov switching treats a change as a probability but risks overfitting and the wrong regime count.
Instead of committing to one regime,
State space → filtering → nonlinearity → HMM → financial application closes the loop.
